correctness.rationale: The connected symmetric graph Laplacian has a simple constant zero mode; the diagonal spectral weights on all positive modes sum to 1-1/n. The scalar extrapolation filter has exactly one positive derivative root and a strictly positive sum-of-squares certificate for R(z)+1/27. These yield the universal sharp infimum and strict positivity through n=28. Equality forces e_i-1/n*1 to lie in one eigenspace, hence all incident conductances equal; conversely such a universal vertex attains the bound at the minimizing step. The exact R(12)=-23/637 star witness rules out all n>=29. A sign-variation argument and intermediate values give precisely two positive zeros of the hub diagonal cubic, with one bounded negative timestep interval. value.rationale: Mass-preserving rational time integrators may exhibit negative self-return coefficients even when the underlying symmetric diffusion semigroup is positive. The finding establishes a universal all-topology cutoff at exactly 28/29 states, not a hand-picked finite instance. Its tight bound is achieved by the sparsest possible connected family (equal-weight stars) and all network vertices that are equally weighted universal hubs, regardless of neighbor-edge geometry. It classifies the entire bounded timestep interval of sign loss and recovery on these vertices. Such structural sharpness and an exact smallest failure dimension constitute a naturally motivated cutoff and a design/diagnostic fact, rather than a restatement of scalar Richardson failure.
